sense: by way of a place or a route

evidence: Vulg. Mt. 2.12: per aliam viam reversī sunt
terms.comment: The way taken, through a land or by a road: per Sēquanōs, through the land of the Sequani; per aliam viam, by another road.

terms.gloss: by (a road, by land, by sea)
terms.grammar: ablative of the way, without a preposition
evidence: Hor. S. 1.9.1: ībam forte viā Sacrā
terms.comment: The road, gate or element one travels by stands in the ablative: viā Appiā, by the Appian Way; portā exīre, go out by the gate; terrā marīque, by land and sea.

phrases.latin: per aliam viam reversī sunt in regiōnem suam
phrases.english: they went back to their own country by another road

phrases.latin: Erant omnīnō itinera duo, quibus itineribus domō exīre possent: ūnum per Sēquanōs, angustum et difficile
phrases.english: there were only two routes by which they could leave home: one via the Sequani, narrow and difficult

phrases.latin: ībam forte viā Sacrā, sīcut meus est mōs
phrases.english: I happened to be going by the Sacred Way, as is my habit
